text: commission appointed inquire loss royal charter steam clipper held sittings liverpool beginning 6 february 1860 before mr. trenenheere, assisted capt harris capt gray board of trade. ship 2,719 tons register, built clyde sandycroft 1855, left melbourne 26 august 1859 w/ 388 passengers, crew 112, general cargo incl 79,000 ounces gold in 39 boxes consigned london banks. commanded capt john taylor, sailed ship since first voyage. after passage 59 days against heavy westerly winds, rounded mull of galloway morning 25 october, took 2 pilots aboard point lynas. evening wind backed northeast, increased hurricane force by 10 o'clock. engines 200 nominal horsepower worked utmost, but ship drifted stern-first toward anglesey coast. half past one morning 26 october struck rocks half mile east moelfre. first boat launched stove against ship's side; raft built carpenter peter gibson carried purser + twenty men shore; buoy line rigged mate joseph rodgers saved further nineteen. total 41 survived of 500 aboard. gold, one exception, went down w/ ship; single box 1,640 ounces recovered beach moelfre november by local man robert williams. commission found ship seaworthy well found; pilots advised standing out sea when wind shifted; decision anchor moelfre roads taken capt taylor against advice. recommended storm signal station point lynas + lifeboat moelfre, both provided within 2 years by marine board.
